sanskrit: prajñāvāṃs tv eva puruṣaḥ saṃyuktaḥ parayā dhiyā udayāstamayajño hi na śocati na hṛṣyati
english: A person who is truly wise, endowed with the highest understanding, who knows the rising and setting of things — he neither grieves nor exults.

sanskrit: sukham āpatitaṃ seved duḥkham āpatitaṃ sahet kālaprāptam upāsīta sasyānām iva karṣakaḥ
english: He should enjoy happiness when it comes and endure suffering when it arrives; he should attend to what the season brings, just as a farmer tends to crops.

sanskrit: tapaso hi paraṃ nāsti tapasā vindate mahat nāsādhyaṃ tapasaḥ kiṃ cid iti budhyasva bhārata
english: There is nothing higher than austerity; through austerity one attains great things. Nothing is unattainable by austerity — understand this, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: satyam ārjavam akrodhaḥ saṃvibhāgo damaḥ śamaḥ anasūyāvihiṃsā ca śaucam indriyasaṃyamaḥ sādhanāni mahārāja narāṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām
english: Truth, straightforwardness, freedom from anger, sharing, self-restraint, tranquility, freedom from envy, non-violence, purity, and control of the senses — these, O great king, are the means of meritorious conduct for men.

sanskrit: adharmarucayo mūḍhās tiryaggatiparāyaṇāḥ kṛcchrāṃ yonim anuprāpya na sukhaṃ vindate janāḥ
english: Those foolish persons who delight in unrighteousness, destined for inferior births, having attained a miserable womb, find no happiness.

sanskrit: iha yat kriyate karma tat paratropabhujyate tasmāc charīraṃ yuñjīta tapasā niyamena ca
english: Whatever deed is done here is experienced in the hereafter; therefore one should employ the body in austerity and observance of vows.

sanskrit: yathāśakti prayacchec ca saṃpūjyābhipraṇamya ca kāle pātre ca hṛṣṭātmā rājan vigatamatsaraḥ
english: One should give according to one's ability, having honoured and reverenced the worthy recipient, at the right time and to the right person, with a joyful heart, O king, free from envy.

sanskrit: satyavādī labhetāyur anāyāsam athārjavī akrodhano 'nasūyaś ca nirvṛtiṃ labhate parām
english: A speaker of truth gains long life; a straightforward person gains it without effort; one free from anger and free from envy attains the highest peace.

sanskrit: dāntaḥ śamaparaḥ śaśvat parikleśaṃ na vindati na ca tapyati dāntātmā dṛṣṭvā paragatāṃ śriyam
english: One who is self-controlled and ever devoted to tranquility does not encounter affliction; nor does the self-controlled soul grieve upon seeing another's prosperity.

sanskrit: saṃvibhaktā ca dātā ca bhogavān sukhavān naraḥ bhavaty ahiṃsakaś caiva paramārogyam aśnute
english: A man who shares and gives enjoys pleasures and happiness; one who is non-violent attains supreme health.

sanskrit: mānyān mānayitā janma kule mahati vindati vyasanair na tu saṃyogaṃ prāpnoti vijitendriyaḥ
english: One who honours those worthy of honour is born in a noble family; one who has conquered the senses does not fall into the company of vices.

sanskrit: śubhānuśayabuddhir hi saṃyuktaḥ kāladharmaṇā prādurbhavati tadyogāt kalyāṇamatir eva saḥ
english: One whose mind tends toward auspicious reflection, united with the law of time, manifests through that union — he is truly a person of noble understanding.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhagavan dānadharmāṇāṃ tapaso vā mahāmune kiṃ svid bahuguṇaṃ pretya kiṃ vā duṣkaram ucyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O blessed one, O great sage, among the virtues of giving, the virtues of dharma, or the practice of austerity, which is said to yield the most fruit after death, or which is said to be the most difficult?

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca dānān na duṣkarataraṃ pṛthivyām asti kiṃ cana arthe hi mahatī tṛṣṇā sa ca duḥkhena labhyate
english: Vyāsa said: There is nothing more difficult than giving on this earth, for the craving for wealth is immense, and wealth itself is obtained only through hardship.

sanskrit: parityajya priyān prāṇān dhanārthaṃ hi mahāhavam praviśanti narā vīrāḥ samudram aṭavīṃ tathā
english: For the sake of wealth, valiant men enter great battles, leaving behind their dear lives; they venture into the ocean and into forests.

sanskrit: kṛṣigorakṣyam ity eke pratipadyanti mānavāḥ puruṣāḥ preṣyatām eke nirgacchanti dhanārthinaḥ
english: Some men resort to agriculture and cattle-rearing; others who desire wealth go out as servants seeking their fortunes.

sanskrit: tasya duḥkhārjitasyaivaṃ parityāgaḥ suduṣkaraḥ na duṣkarataraṃ dānāt tasmād dānaṃ mataṃ mama
english: To give up wealth thus earned with such suffering is extremely difficult; therefore there is nothing more difficult than giving — that is my view.

sanskrit: viśeṣas tv atra vijñeyo nyāyenopārjitaṃ dhanam pātre deśe ca kāle ca sādhubhyaḥ pratipādayet
english: Yet a distinction must be understood here: wealth righteously earned should be given to worthy persons, in the right place and at the right time.

sanskrit: anyāyasamupāttena dānadharmo dhanena yaḥ kriyate na sa kartāraṃ trāyate mahato bhayāt
english: The dharma of giving performed with wealth unjustly acquired does not protect its doer from great fear.

sanskrit: pātre dānaṃ svalpam api kāle dattaṃ yudhiṣṭhira manasā suviśuddhena pretyānantaphalaṃ smṛtam
english: Even a small gift given to a worthy recipient at the right time, O Yudhiṣṭhira, with a perfectly pure mind, is remembered as yielding infinite fruit after death.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam vrīhidroṇaparityāgād yat phalaṃ prāpa mudgalaḥ
english: On this subject they also cite this ancient story — the fruit that Mudgala obtained by giving away a measure of rice.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vrīhidroṇaḥ parityaktaḥ kathaṃ tena mahātmanā kasmai dattaś ca bhagavan vidhinā kena cāttha me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was that measure of rice given up by that great soul? To whom was it given, O blessed one, and by what rite? Tell me this.

sanskrit: pratyakṣadharmā bhagavān yasya tuṣṭo hi karmabhiḥ saphalaṃ tasya janmāhaṃ manye saddharmacāriṇaḥ
english: You, O blessed one, are one who sees dharma directly. I consider fruitful the birth of that practitioner of true dharma whose actions have pleased you.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca śiloñchavṛttir dharmātmā mudgalaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ āsīd rājan kurukṣetre satyavāg anasūyakaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: O king, there was Mudgala, a man of righteous soul and sharpened vows, who lived by gleaning grain from the fields; he dwelt in Kurukṣetra, a speaker of truth, free from envy.

sanskrit: atithivratī kriyāvāṃś ca kāpotīṃ vṛttim āsthitaḥ satram iṣṭīkṛtaṃ nāma samupāste mahātapāḥ
english: Devoted to the vow of hospitality and active in rites, he had adopted the pigeon's way of living; the great ascetic performed the sacrifice known as Ishtikrita.

sanskrit: saputradāro hi muniḥ pakṣāhāro babhūva saḥ kapotavṛttyā pakṣeṇa vrīhidroṇam upārjayat
english: The sage, together with his sons and wife, ate only once a fortnight; living by the pigeon's gleaning, he gathered a measure of rice over a fortnight.

sanskrit: darśaṃ ca paurṇamāsaṃ ca kurvan vigatamatsaraḥ devatātithiśeṣeṇa kurute dehayāpanam
english: Performing the new-moon and full-moon rites, free from envy, he sustained his body on what remained after the gods and guests had been served.

sanskrit: tasyendraḥ sahito devaiḥ sākṣāt tribhuvaneśvaraḥ pratyagṛhṇān mahārāja bhāgaṃ parvaṇi parvaṇi
english: Indra himself, together with the gods, the lord of the three worlds in person, would receive his portion at each lunar observance, O great king.

sanskrit: sa parvakālaṃ kṛtvā tu munivṛttyā samanvitaḥ atithibhyo dadāv annaṃ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
english: Having completed the sacred occasion with a sage's conduct, he gave food to guests with a heart overflowing with joy.

sanskrit: vrīhidroṇasya tadaho dadato 'nnaṃ mahātmanaḥ śiṣṭaṃ mātsaryahīnasya vardhaty atithidarśanāt
english: On that day, as the great-souled one gave out food from his measure of rice, the remainder — of one who was free from envy — increased at the sight of each guest.

sanskrit: tac chatāny api bhuñjanti brāhmaṇānāṃ manīṣiṇām munes tyāgaviśuddhyā tu tadannaṃ vṛddhim ṛcchati
english: Even hundreds of wise brahmins would eat of it; through the purity of the sage's renunciation, that food kept multiplying.

sanskrit: taṃ tu śuśrāva dharmiṣṭhaṃ mudgalaṃ saṃśitavratam durvāsā nṛpa digvāsās tam athābhyājagāma ha
english: Then Durvāsā — the sky-clad sage, O king — heard of that most righteous Mudgala of sharpened vow, and came to him.

sanskrit: bibhrac cāniyataṃ veṣam unmatta iva pāṇḍava vikacaḥ paruṣā vāco vyāharan vividhā muniḥ
english: The sage wore an irregular garb, O Pāṇḍava; he appeared like a madman, his hair dishevelled, uttering various harsh words.

sanskrit: abhigamyātha taṃ vipram uvāca munisattamaḥ annārthinam anuprāptaṃ viddhi māṃ munisattama
english: Approaching that brahmin, the great sage said: Know me, O best of sages, as one who has come seeking food.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ te 'stv iti muniṃ mudgalaḥ pratyabhāṣata pādyam ācamanīyaṃ ca prativedyānnam uttamam
english: "You are welcome" — so Mudgala addressed the sage, and offered water for the feet, water for sipping, and then the finest food.

sanskrit: prādāt sa tapasopāttaṃ kṣudhitāyātithivratī unmattāya parāṃ śraddhām āsthāya sa dhṛtavrataḥ
english: He who was pledged to hospitality, steadfast in his vow, gave to the hungry and seemingly mad guest that food earned through austerity, with supreme faith.

sanskrit: tatas tadannaṃ rasavat sa eva kṣudhayānvitaḥ bubhuje kṛtsnam unmattaḥ prādāt tasmai ca mudgalaḥ
english: Then that mad one, filled with hunger, ate all of that savory food himself; and Mudgala gave it entirely to him.

sanskrit: bhuktvā cānnaṃ tataḥ sarvam ucchiṣṭenātmanas tataḥ athānulilipe 'ṅgāni jagāma ca yathāgatam
english: Having eaten all the food, he then smeared his own body with the leavings, and departed just as he had come.

sanskrit: evaṃ dvitīye saṃprāpte parvakāle manīṣiṇaḥ āgamya bubhuje sarvam annam uñchopajīvinaḥ
english: In this same manner, when the second lunar observance arrived, that wise one came again and ate all the food of the one who lived by gleaning.

sanskrit: nirāhāras tu sa munir uñcham ārjayate punaḥ na cainaṃ vikriyāṃ netum aśakan mudgalaṃ kṣudhā
english: The sage, left without food, would go out gleaning again; and hunger was unable to bring any agitation in Mudgala.

sanskrit: na krodho na ca mātsaryaṃ nāvamāno na saṃbhramaḥ saputradāram uñchantam āviveśa dvijottamam
english: Neither anger, nor envy, nor contempt, nor confusion entered that best of twice-born ones as he gleaned with his sons and wife.

sanskrit: tathā tam uñchadharmāṇaṃ durvāsā munisattamam upatasthe yathākālaṃ ṣaṭkṛtvaḥ kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: In this same way, Durvāsā, that foremost of sages, with firm resolve, tested that practitioner of the gleaning-dharma six times at the proper occasion.

sanskrit: na cāsya mānasaṃ kiṃ cid vikāraṃ dadṛśe muniḥ śuddhasattvasya śuddhaṃ sa dadṛśe nirmalaṃ manaḥ
english: The sage found not the slightest perturbation in his mind; he saw the pure, stainless mind of one whose nature was wholly pure.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tataḥ prītaḥ sa munir mudgalaṃ tadā tvatsamo nāsti loke 'smin dātā mātsaryavarjitaḥ
english: Then that sage, filled with joy, spoke to Mudgala: "There is no giver in this world equal to you, who is utterly free from envy."

sanskrit: kṣud dharmasaṃjñāṃ praṇudaty ādatte dhairyam eva ca viṣayānusāriṇī jihvā karṣaty eva rasān prati
english: Hunger drives away the awareness of dharma and takes away even steadiness; the tongue, following sense-objects, drags one toward tastes.

sanskrit: āhāraprabhavāḥ prāṇā mano durnigrahaṃ calam manasaś cendriyāṇāṃ cāpy aikāgryaṃ niścitaṃ tapaḥ
english: The vital breaths are sustained by food; the mind is difficult to restrain and restless; and the one-pointed concentration of the mind and senses — that is truly what is meant by austerity.

sanskrit: śrameṇopārjitaṃ tyaktuṃ duḥkhaṃ śuddhena cetasā tat sarvaṃ bhavatā sādho yathāvad upapāditam
english: To give up with a pure heart what has been earned with such effort and pain — all that has been perfectly accomplished by you, O virtuous one.

sanskrit: prītāḥ smo 'nugṛhītāś ca sametya bhavatā saha indriyābhijayo dhairyaṃ saṃvibhāgo damaḥ śamaḥ
english: We are pleased and feel honoured to have met with you; the conquest of the senses, steadiness, sharing, self-restraint, and tranquility —

sanskrit: dayā satyaṃ ca dharmaś ca tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam jitās te karmabhir lokāḥ prāpto 'si paramāṃ gatim
english: — compassion, truth, and dharma — all these are established in you. The worlds have been won by your deeds; you have attained the supreme destination.

sanskrit: aho dānaṃ vighuṣṭaṃ te sumahat svargavāsibhiḥ saśarīro bhavān gantā svargaṃ sucaritavrata
english: Ah, how greatly your act of giving is proclaimed by the dwellers of heaven! You, O one of noble vow, shall ascend to heaven in your own body.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vadatas tasya tadā durvāsaso muneḥ devadūto vimānena mudgalaṃ pratyupasthitaḥ
english: While sage Durvāsā was saying these very words, a divine messenger arrived before Mudgala in a celestial chariot.

sanskrit: haṃsasārasayuktena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā kāmagena vicitreṇa divyagandhavatā tathā
english: It was yoked with swans and cranes, garlanded with networks of tinkling bells, moving at will, wondrous in its beauty, fragrant with divine scents.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ viprarṣiṃ vimānaṃ karmabhir jitam samupāroha saṃsiddhiṃ prāpto 'si paramāṃ mune
english: He spoke to that brahmin-sage: "This celestial chariot has been won by your deeds — ascend it. You have attained the highest perfection, O sage."

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinam ṛṣir devadūtam uvāca ha icchāmi bhavatā proktān guṇān svarganivāsinām
english: The sage spoke to that divine messenger who had spoken thus: "I wish to hear from you the qualities of those who dwell in heaven."

sanskrit: ke guṇās tatra vasatāṃ kiṃ tapaḥ kaś ca niścayaḥ svarge svargasukhaṃ kiṃ ca doṣo vā devadūtaka
english: "What are the virtues of those who dwell there? What is the austerity, what the resolve? What is the happiness of heaven? And what, O divine messenger, are its faults?"

sanskrit: satāṃ saptapadaṃ mitram āhuḥ santaḥ kulocitāḥ mitratāṃ ca puraskṛtya pṛcchāmi tvām ahaṃ vibho
english: "The virtuous, those established in a noble lineage, say that seven steps together make a friendship. Honouring that friendship, I ask you, O lord."

sanskrit: yad atra tathyaṃ pathyaṃ ca tad bravīhy avicārayan śrutvā tathā kariṣyāmi vyavasāyaṃ girā tava
english: "Whatever is true and beneficial in this matter, speak it without hesitation; having heard, I shall act accordingly by the resolution your words inspire."

sanskrit: devadūta uvāca maharṣe 'kāryabuddhis tvaṃ yaḥ svargasukham uttamam saṃprāptaṃ bahu mantavyaṃ vimṛśasy abudho yathā
english: The divine messenger said: O great sage, you are acting without discernment — like an ignorant person, you are deliberating over the supreme happiness of heaven that has been placed before you.

sanskrit: upariṣṭād asau loko yo 'yaṃ svar iti saṃjñitaḥ ūrdhvagaḥ satpathaḥ śaśvad devayānacaro mune
english: That world above, known by the name Svarga — heaven — is the ever-upward path, the good path, eternally traversed by the way of the gods, O sage.

sanskrit: nātaptatapasaḥ puṃso nāmahāyajñayājinaḥ nānṛtā nāstikāś caiva tatra gacchanti mudgala
english: Those who have not heated themselves with austerity, those who have not performed great sacrifices, the dishonest and the faithless — they do not go there, O Mudgala.

sanskrit: dharmātmāno jitātmānaḥ śāntā dāntā vimatsarāḥ dānadharmaratāḥ puṃsaḥ śūrāś cāhatalakṣaṇāḥ
english: Those whose souls are righteous, who have conquered themselves, who are peaceful and self-controlled and free from envy, who delight in the dharma of giving, who are heroes bearing auspicious marks —

sanskrit: tatra gacchanti karmāgryaṃ kṛtvā śamadamātmakam lokān puṇyakṛtāṃ brahman sadbhir āsevitān nṛbhiḥ
english: — they go there, having performed the highest deeds of restraint and self-control, to those worlds of the meritorious, O brahmin, frequented by virtuous men.

sanskrit: devāḥ sādhyās tathā viśve marutaś ca maharṣibhiḥ yāmā dhāmāś ca maudgalya gandharvāpsarasas tathā
english: The gods, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the Maruts along with the great sages, the Yamas, the Dhamas, O Mudgala, and the Gandharvas and Apsaras —

sanskrit: eṣāṃ devanikāyānāṃ pṛthak pṛthag anekaśaḥ bhāsvantaḥ kāmasaṃpannā lokās tejomayāḥ śubhāḥ
english: — for each of these groups of gods there are many separate worlds, radiant, fulfilling all desires, made of light, auspicious.

sanskrit: trayastriṃśat sahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ hiraṇmayaḥ meruḥ parvatarāḍ yatra devodyānāni mudgala
english: Meru, the king of mountains, golden, thirty-three thousand yojanas in extent — there the divine gardens are found, O Mudgala.

sanskrit: nandanādīni puṇyāni vihārāḥ puṇyakarmaṇām na kṣutpipāse na glānir na śītoṣṇabhayaṃ tathā
english: Nandana and other sacred groves, the pleasure-grounds of those of meritorious deeds — there is no hunger, no thirst, no weariness, no fear of cold or heat.

sanskrit: bībhatsam aśubhaṃ vāpi rogā vā tatra ke cana manojñāḥ sarvato gandhāḥ sukhasparśāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Nothing disgusting or inauspicious, no diseases of any kind — on all sides are charming fragrances, and pleasant sensations everywhere.

sanskrit: śabdāḥ śrutimanogrāhyāḥ sarvatas tatra vai mune na śoko na jarā tatra nāyāsaparidevane
english: Sounds that delight both the ear and the mind are everywhere there, O sage. There is no grief, no old age, no toil, no lamentation.

sanskrit: īdṛśaḥ sa mune lokaḥ svakarmaphalahetukaḥ sukṛtais tatra puruṣāḥ saṃbhavanty ātmakarmabhiḥ
english: Such is that world, O sage, caused by the fruit of one's own deeds; men of good deeds come to be there by their own actions.

sanskrit: taijasāni śarīrāṇi bhavanty atropapadyatām karmajāny eva maudgalya na mātṛpitṛjāny uta
english: The bodies acquired by those who go there, O Mudgala, are made of light and born of karma alone — not of mother and father.

sanskrit: na ca svedo na daurgandhyaṃ purīṣaṃ mūtram eva ca teṣāṃ na ca rajo vastraṃ bādhate tatra vai mune
english: There is no sweat, no foul odour, no excrement, no urine for those beings there, O sage; dust does not soil their garments.

sanskrit: na mlāyanti srajas teṣāṃ divyagandhā manoramāḥ paryuhyante vimānaiś ca brahmann evaṃvidhāś ca te
english: Their garlands of divine, mind-delighting fragrance do not wilt; they are surrounded by celestial chariots — such indeed are those beings, O brahmin.

sanskrit: īrṣyāśokaklamāpetā mohamātsaryavarjitāḥ sukhaṃ svargajitas tatra vartayanti mahāmune
english: Free from envy, grief, and exhaustion, bereft of delusion and jealousy, those who have won heaven live there in happiness, O great sage.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tathāvidhānāṃ tu lokānāṃ munipuṃgava upary upari śakrasya lokā divyaguṇānvitāḥ
english: Above those worlds of such beings, O bull among sages, are the worlds of Śakra, endowed with divine qualities, layer upon layer.

sanskrit: purastād brahmaṇas tatra lokās tejomayāḥ śubhāḥ yatra yānty ṛṣayo brahman pūtāḥ svaiḥ karmabhiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: Before Brahmā there are those luminous, auspicious worlds where the sages go, O brahmin, purified by their own meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: ṛbhavo nāma tatrānye devānām api devatāḥ teṣāṃ lokāḥ paratare tān yajantīha devatāḥ
english: There are others known as the Ribhus — gods even among gods; their worlds are beyond those others, and the gods themselves worship them here.

sanskrit: svayaṃprabhās te bhāsvanto lokāḥ kāmadughāḥ pare na teṣāṃ strīkṛtas tāpo na lokaiśvaryamatsaraḥ
english: Those worlds are self-luminous, radiant, and yield all desires; for those beings there is no torment caused by women, no jealousy over the lordship of worlds.

sanskrit: na vartayanty āhutibhis te nāpy amṛtabhojanāḥ tathā divyaśarīrās te na ca vigrahamūrtayaḥ
english: They do not sustain themselves through oblations, nor do they feed on ambrosia; likewise they possess divine bodies and are not embodied in forms that conflict with one another.

sanskrit: na sukhe sukhakāmāś ca devadevāḥ sanātanāḥ na kalpaparivarteṣu parivartanti te tathā
english: Those eternal gods of gods do not even desire happiness in happiness; they do not revolve through the cycles of cosmic ages as others do.

sanskrit: jarā mṛtyuḥ kutas teṣāṃ harṣaḥ prītiḥ sukhaṃ na ca na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ cāpi rāgadveṣau kuto mune
english: Where would old age or death be for them? There is no elation, no joy, no pleasure — and no sorrow, no happiness either. Where would attachment and aversion be, O sage?
